raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Add a `w4afp8` quantization method so SGLang-style W4AFP8 MoE checkpoints (`PhalaCloud/GLM-5.3-W4AFP8`) can be served by reusing the compressed-tensors W4A8 FP8 MoE path from #58427. Load-time layout translation only: no kernel, C++, or build changes.

## Claims

- `PhalaCloud/GLM-5.3-W4AFP8` loads and serves end-to-end on 8x H20 (TP=8 + EP=8) driven by the checkpoint's own `quant_method`, scoring GSM8K 0.9113 against the 0.911 reported for `gpustack/GLM-5.3-W4A8` in #58427.
- Routed experts reuse the Humming / CUTLASS W4A8 oracle; the on-disk differences are translated at load time (signed INT4 -> `uint4b8`, `int8` pack=2 -> `int32` pack=8, `*_scale_inv` -> `*_scale`, static `w{1,2,3}.input_scale` dropped), while dense `Linear` layers use the native `Fp8Config` block-128 path, which already expects `weight_scale_inv`.
- Core impact is `+24` additive lines in `routed_experts.py` behind a flag defaulting to `False`; no existing quantization path changes behavior.

## Validation

```bash
pytest tests/quantization/test_w4afp8.py -v      # 7 passed, CPU only

vllm serve PhalaCloud/GLM-5.3-W4AFP8 --tensor-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel --trust-remote-code --max-model-len 2048 --enforce-eager --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla --gpu-memory-utilization 0.80 --moe-backend humming

python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --num-questions 1319 --num-shots 5 --max-tokens 256 --temperature 0.0 --seed 42 --max-concurrency 128
```

GSM8K, 1,319 questions, 5-shot, `temperature=0`, `seed=42`, single run per backend:

| Config | Accuracy | QPS | Output tokens/s | Baseline (#58427) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--moe-backend humming` | **0.9113** (1202/1319) | 5.07 | 489.6 | 0.911 |
| `--moe-backend cutlass` | 0.9113 (1202/1319) | 5.33 | 515.0 | n/a |

Both backends produce coherent output on English, arithmetic and Chinese prompts, every checkpoint tensor loads with no `KeyError`, and pre-commit (ruff, pyright, isort) passes on the touched files.

## Details

**Why an adapter.** Only the serialization differs, so the change is a `CompressedTensorsW4A8Fp8MoEMethod` subclass plus a `CompressedTensorsConfig` subclass. Parameters are created under the checkpoint's own names and widths so the stock expert-parameter mapping loader fills them; `process_weights_after_loading` repacks and defers to the parent, which runs the kernel-format conversion, backend selection and kernel construction unchanged. Editing the shared parent instead would put the `gpustack/GLM-5.3-W4A8` path at risk of regressions.

**Format translation.** The checkpoint stores two's-complement signed INT4, two nibbles per `int8` byte, while the kernels consume `uint4b8`; XOR-ing each byte with `0x88` adds 8 to both nibbles at once, then `view(torch.int32)` folds four bytes into one word. The repack is a pure tensor function, so it is unit-tested without a GPU.

**Static activation scales.** The W4A8 kernels recompute activation scales per token, so `w{1,2,3}.input_scale` is loaded (a parameter has to exist for the loader) and then retired via `retire_parameter`, which keeps it registered for weight reloading while hiding it from the kernels. Because it is never consumed, the fused parameter holds one scalar per expert (`[E]`) instead of ModelOpt's `[E, 2]`, which is what keeps the `routed_experts.py` change purely additive. Renamed and retired parameters follow the convention introduced in #62407 (`move_parameter` / `retire_parameter`). Layers whose expert naming does not match the config regex would silently stay unquantized, so `get_quant_method` warns in that case.

**Scope.** Group size 128 with symmetric INT4; hidden size and per-partition intermediate size must be multiples of 256; on-disk static scales are ignored by design; validated on H20 (SM90) only.

**Prior art.** #53848 (closed) attempted the same checkpoint support by integrating the conversion into the Humming fused-MoE experts; it was abandoned with unresolved merge conflicts. This PR keeps the conversion out of the kernel path and reuses the compressed-tensors W4A8 oracle instead. #49979 (closed) proposed a dedicated SM90 grouped-MoE kernel and was directed to this oracle path as well. No other open PR targets this quant method.

+# W4AFP8
+
+`w4afp8` is a mixed-precision format for Mixture-of-Experts models: routed
+expert weights are INT4 (group size 128) while activations stay in FP8, and
+dense `Linear` layers are FP8 block-128 (W8A8).
+
+vLLM supports the variant published by PhalaCloud, where
+`config.json` declares `"quant_method": "w4afp8"`. `PhalaCloud/GLM-5.3-W4AFP8`
+is the reference checkpoint.
+
+## Usage
+
+```bash
+vllm serve PhalaCloud/GLM-5.3-W4AFP8 \
+  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
+  --enable-expert-parallel \
+  --trust-remote-code \
+  --moe-backend humming
+```
+
+`--moe-backend` accepts `humming` or `cutlass`. On SM90 with aligned shapes
+(hidden size and per-partition intermediate size divisible by 256) `cutlass` is
+selected automatically.
+
+## How it works
+
+No dedicated kernel is involved. The loader translates the on-disk layout at
+load time and then reuses the compressed-tensors W4A8 FP8 MoE path
+(the Humming / CUTLASS W4A8 oracle):
+
+| On disk | vLLM / kernel expects |
+| --- | --- |
+| signed INT4, two nibbles per byte | `uint4b8`, offset-by-8 unsigned INT4 |
+| `int8` pack=2 | `int32` pack=8 |
+| `*_proj.weight_scale_inv` | `*_weight_scale` |
+| `w{1,2,3}.input_scale` (static) | dropped; per-token dynamic FP8 scales |
+
+Dense layers already match the native FP8 block-128 serialization
+(`weight_scale_inv`), so they are loaded by the regular `fp8` path.
+
+## Limitations
+
+- Group size must be 128 and weights must be symmetric INT4.
+- Hidden size and the per-partition intermediate size must be multiples of 256.
+- Static per-tensor activation scales in the checkpoint are ignored: the W4A8
+  FP8 kernels recompute activation scales per token.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""CPU-only unit tests for the ``w4afp8`` layout translation.
+
+Run `pytest tests/quantization/test_w4afp8.py`.
+
+These tests cover the on-disk repack (signed INT4 -> ``uint4b8``) and the
+configuration wiring. Whether the W4A8 kernel consumes the resulting tensor
+correctly needs a GPU end-to-end run and is out of scope here.
+"""
+
+import sys
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.w4afp8 import (
+    W4AFP8Config,
+    _repack_signed_int4_to_uint4b8,
+)
+
+
+def _pack_nibbles(nibbles: list[int]) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Pack 4-bit patterns two per byte, low nibble first."""
+    assert len(nibbles) % 2 == 0
+    payload = [nibbles[i] | (nibbles[i + 1] << 4) for i in range(0, len(nibbles), 2)]
+    return torch.tensor([payload], dtype=torch.uint8).view(torch.int8)
+
+
+def _unpack_nibbles(bytes_: torch.Tensor) -> list[int]:
+    """Inverse of `_pack_nibbles` for a byte view of the repacked tensor."""
+    return [
+        nibble
+        for byte in bytes_.flatten().tolist()
+        for nibble in (byte & 0xF, (byte >> 4) & 0xF)
+    ]
+
+
+def test_repack_known_bytes():
+    # int4 payloads -> packed bytes 0x88, 0xF1, 0x7F, 0x00 (one int32 word).
+    packed = _pack_nibbles([0x8, 0x8, 0x1, 0xF, 0xF, 0x7, 0x0, 0x0])
+
+    out = _repack_signed_int4_to_uint4b8(packed)
+
+    assert out.dtype is torch.int32
+    assert out.shape == (1, packed.shape[-1] // 4)
+    words = out.view(torch.uint8).reshape(-1, 4)
+    if sys.byteorder == "big":
+        words = words.flip(-1)
+    assert words.flatten().tolist() == [0x00, 0x79, 0xF7, 0x88]
+
+
+def test_repack_shifts_every_nibble_by_eight():
+    nibbles = list(range(16)) * 2  # all 16 int4 payloads, 32 nibbles = 4 words
+
+    out = _repack_signed_int4_to_uint4b8(_pack_nibbles(nibbles))
+
+    # A word holds 4 consecutive bytes; undo the per-word byte order so the
+    # assertion does not depend on the host's endianness.
+    words = out.view(torch.uint8).reshape(-1, 4)
+    if sys.byteorder == "big":
+        words = words.flip(-1)
+    assert _unpack_nibbles(words) == [(value + 8) % 16 for value in nibbles]
+
+
+def test_repack_leaves_input_untouched():
+    packed = _pack_nibbles([0x1, 0x2, 0x3, 0x4, 0x5, 0x6, 0x7, 0x8])
+    before = packed.clone()
+
+    _repack_signed_int4_to_uint4b8(packed)
+
+    assert torch.equal(packed, before)
+
+
+def test_repack_rejects_non_int8():
+    with pytest.raises(AssertionError):
+        _repack_signed_int4_to_uint4b8(torch.zeros(1, 4, dtype=torch.int32))
+
+
+def test_repack_rejects_partial_word():
+    with pytest.raises(AssertionError):
+        _repack_signed_int4_to_uint4b8(torch.zeros(1, 6, dtype=torch.int8))
+
+
+def test_config_name_and_dense_dispatch():
+    assert W4AFP8Config.get_name() == "w4afp8"
+
+    config = W4AFP8Config.from_config(
+        {
+            "quant_method": "w4afp8",
+            "group_size": 128,
+            "modules_to_not_convert": ["lm_head"],
+        }
+    )
+
+    # Dense layers must go through the native FP8 block-128 path, because these
+    # checkpoints name the block scale `weight_scale_inv`.
+    dense = config._dense_fp8_config
+    assert dense.is_checkpoint_fp8_serialized
+    assert dense.activation_scheme == "dynamic"
+    assert dense.weight_block_size == [128, 128]
+    assert dense.ignored_layers == ["lm_head"]
+
+
+def test_config_rejects_other_quant_method():
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="w4afp8"):
+        W4AFP8Config.from_config({"quant_method": "compressed-tensors"})

@@ -0,0 +1,307 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""``w4afp8`` quantization: PhalaCloud W4A8 MoE checkpoints.
+
+Routed experts are translated into the compressed-tensors W4A8 FP8 MoE path
+(Humming / CUTLASS W4A8 oracle, vllm-project/vllm#58427), so no kernel or
+build changes are involved. Dense Linear layers reuse the native FP8
+block-128 path, because these checkpoints serialize dense scales under
+``weight_scale_inv`` (as :class:`Fp8Config` expects) rather than
+``weight_scale``.
+
+Per routed expert the checkpoint (e.g. ``PhalaCloud/GLM-5.3-W4AFP8``) holds:
+
+* ``{gate,up,down}_proj.weight``: signed INT4, two nibbles per ``int8`` byte.
+* ``{gate,up,down}_proj.weight_scale_inv``: ``bf16`` group-128 scales.
+* ``w{1,2,3}.input_scale``: static per-tensor FP8 activation scales, loaded
+  only so that the stock loader finds a parameter for them. The W4A8 FP8
+  kernels consume dynamic per-token activations, so the values are dropped.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any, cast
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe import (
+    FusedMoeWeightScaleSupported,
+    RoutedExperts,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.config import FusedMoEConfig
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization import QuantizationMethods
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.compressed_tensors.compressed_tensors import (  # noqa: E501
+    CompressedTensorsConfig,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.compressed_tensors.compressed_tensors_moe.compressed_tensors_moe_w4a8_fp8 import (  # noqa: E501
+    CompressedTensorsW4A8Fp8MoEMethod,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.fp8 import Fp8Config
+from vllm.model_executor.utils import (
+    move_parameter,
+    replace_parameter,
+    retire_parameter,
+    set_weight_attrs,
+)
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from compressed_tensors.quantization import QuantizationArgs
+
+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.base_config import (
+        QuantizeMethodBase,
+    )
+    from vllm.model_executor.models.utils import WeightsMapper
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+# Routed experts of GLM/DeepSeek-style checkpoints. Layers that do not match
+# stay unquantized, which is why `get_quant_method` warns instead of silently
+# accepting them.
+_MOE_EXPERTS_TARGET = r"re:.*\.mlp\.experts\.\d+\.(gate_proj|up_proj|down_proj)$"
+
+# Checkpoint packs two INT4 nibbles per byte; the W4A8 oracle packs eight per
+# int32 word (4 bytes).
+_INT4_PER_BYTE = 2
+
+
+def _repack_signed_int4_to_uint4b8(weight: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Repack signed INT4 (``int8``, 2 per byte) into ``uint4b8`` (``int32``).
+
+    XOR-ing every byte with ``0x88`` flips the sign bit of both nibbles, which
+    maps each two's-complement int4 value ``v`` to ``v + 8`` modulo 16, i.e.
+    the offset-by-8 unsigned encoding the W4A8 MoE kernels consume
+    (compressed-tensors publishes such checkpoints directly, which is why the
+    oracle performs no conversion of its own). ``view(torch.int32)`` then
+    folds the trailing byte axis by four without disturbing those bits.
+    """
+    assert weight.dtype is torch.int8, f"expected int8 weights, got {weight.dtype}"
+    flipped = weight.clone().view(torch.uint8)
+    assert flipped.shape[-1] % 4 == 0, (
+        f"trailing dim {flipped.shape[-1]} does not pack into whole int32 words"
+    )
+    flipped.bitwise_xor_(0x88)
+    return flipped.view(torch.int32)
+
+
+class _W4AFP8MoEAdapter(CompressedTensorsW4A8Fp8MoEMethod):
+    """Bridge the on-disk ``w4afp8`` MoE layout to the W4A8 FP8 path.
+
+    Parameters are created under the checkpoint's own names and widths
+    (``w{13,2}_weight`` as ``int8`` pack=2, ``w{13,2}_weight_scale_inv``,
+    ``w{13,2}_input_scale``) so that the stock
+    ``fused_moe_make_expert_params_mapping`` loader can fill them without any
+    model-side change. :meth:`process_weights_after_loading` then repacks them
+    into the ``int32`` pack=8 / ``*_weight_scale`` layout and hands the layer
+    to the parent, which runs the usual oracle / backend / kernel setup.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        weight_quant: QuantizationArgs,
+        input_quant: QuantizationArgs,
+        moe: FusedMoEConfig,
+        layer_name: str | None = None,
+    ):
+        super().__init__(weight_quant, input_quant, moe, layer_name)
+        # The repack below assumes the parent consumes 8xint4 per int32.
+        assert self.packed_factor == 8, (
+            f"expected 8 int4 per int32, got packed_factor={self.packed_factor}"
+        )
+
+    def create_weights(  # type: ignore[override]
+        self,
+        layer: RoutedExperts,
+        num_experts: int,
+        hidden_size: int,
+        intermediate_size_per_partition: int,
+        params_dtype: torch.dtype,
+        **extra_weight_attrs,
+    ) -> None:
+        layer.num_experts = num_experts
+        layer.orig_dtype = params_dtype
+        layer.weight_block_size = None
+
+        # CUTLASS reorder_tensor requires 256-alignment on both axes.
+        assert hidden_size % 256 == 0, f"{hidden_size=} must be divisible by 256"
+        assert intermediate_size_per_partition % 256 == 0, (
+            f"{intermediate_size_per_partition=} must be divisible by 256"
+        )
+
+        inter = intermediate_size_per_partition
+        n_out = self.moe.w13_num_shards * inter
+
+        # int8 pack=2 signed INT4, as published by PhalaCloud.
+        for name, shape in (
+            ("w13_weight", (num_experts, n_out, hidden_size // _INT4_PER_BYTE)),
+            ("w2_weight", (num_experts, hidden_size, inter // _INT4_PER_BYTE)),
+        ):
+            param = torch.nn.Parameter(
+                torch.empty(shape, dtype=torch.int8), requires_grad=False
+            )
+            layer.register_parameter(name, param)
+            set_weight_attrs(param, extra_weight_attrs)
+
+        per_group = {"quant_method": FusedMoeWeightScaleSupported.GROUP.value}
+        for name, shape, attrs in (
+            (
+                "w13_weight_scale_inv",
+                (num_experts, n_out, hidden_size // self.group_size),
+                per_group,
+            ),
+            (
+                "w2_weight_scale_inv",
+                (num_experts, hidden_size, inter // self.group_size),
+                per_group,
+            ),
+            # Static activation scales: one scalar per expert. `<E>` (not
+            # `<E, 2>`) is enough because w1 and w3 overwrite each other and
+            # the value is discarded after loading anyway.
+            ("w13_input_scale", (num_experts,), {"is_w4afp8_input_scale": True}),
+            ("w2_input_scale", (num_experts,), {"is_w4afp8_input_scale": True}),
+        ):
+            param = torch.nn.Parameter(
+                torch.ones(shape, dtype=params_dtype), requires_grad=False
+            )
+            layer.register_parameter(name, param)
+            set_weight_attrs(param, {**extra_weight_attrs, **attrs})
+
+    def process_weights_after_loading(self, layer: RoutedExperts) -> None:  # type: ignore[override]
+        for name in ("w13", "w2"):
+            replace_parameter(
+                layer,
+                f"{name}_weight",
+                _repack_signed_int4_to_uint4b8(getattr(layer, f"{name}_weight").data),
+            )
+            # The parent reads `*_weight_packed` and aliases it back onto
+            # `*_weight`. Keep the checkpoint name registered as well, so a
+            # later reload still loads through it.
+            move_parameter(layer, f"{name}_weight", f"{name}_weight_packed")
+
+            # `*_scale_inv` -> `*_scale`: same data, the oracle's name. Aliased
+            # rather than renamed, for the same reload reason.
+            move_parameter(layer, f"{name}_weight_scale_inv", f"{name}_weight_scale")
+
+        # Static activation scales are never read by the W4A8 kernels. Retire
+        # them instead of deleting, so reloading stays possible.
+        retire_parameter(layer, "w13_input_scale")
+        retire_parameter(layer, "w2_input_scale")
+        super().process_weights_after_loading(layer)
+
+
+class W4AFP8Config(CompressedTensorsConfig):
+    """Config for ``w4afp8`` checkpoints.
+
+    Inheriting from :class:`CompressedTensorsConfig` keeps the routed-expert
+    plumbing (scheme lookup, backend selection, W4A8 oracle, kernel
+    construction) untouched; only :meth:`from_config`, :meth:`apply_vllm_mapper`
+    and :meth:`get_quant_method` are overridden to pick the right method per
+    layer type.
+    """
+
+    _dense_fp8_config: Fp8Config
+
+    @classmethod
+    def get_name(cls) -> QuantizationMethods:
+        return "w4afp8"
+
+    @classmethod
+    def from_config(cls, config: dict[str, Any]) -> W4AFP8Config:
+        if config.get("quant_method") != "w4afp8":
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"Expected quant_method='w4afp8', got {config.get('quant_method')!r}"
+            )
+
+        group_size = int(config.get("group_size", 128))
+        ignore = list(
+            config.get("modules_to_not_convert") or config.get("ignore") or []
+        )
+
+        # Fabricate the compressed-tensors view of the *routed experts* only;
+        # dense Linear layers are handled by `_dense_fp8_config` below.
+        experts_config = {
+            "quant_method": "compressed-tensors",
+            "format": "pack-quantized",
+            "quantization_status": "compressed",
+            "ignore": ignore,
+            "config_groups": {
+                "group_0": {
+                    "targets": [_MOE_EXPERTS_TARGET],
+                    "format": "pack-quantized",
+                    "weights": {
+                        "num_bits": 4,
+                        "type": "int",
+                        "symmetric": True,
+                        "strategy": "group",
+                        "group_size": group_size,
+                        "dynamic": False,
+                        "observer": "minmax",
+                    },
+                    "input_activations": {
+                        "num_bits": 8,
+                        "type": "float",
+                        "symmetric": True,
+                        "strategy": "token",
+                        "dynamic": True,
+                        "observer": None,
+                    },
+                },
+            },
+        }
+
+        inst = cast("W4AFP8Config", super().from_config(experts_config))
+
+        # Dense layers are FP8 block-128 w8a8 with `weight_scale_inv`, which is
+        # exactly the native FP8 serialization format.
+        inst._dense_fp8_config = Fp8Config(
+            is_checkpoint_fp8_serialized=True,
+            activation_scheme="dynamic",
+            ignored_layers=ignore,
+            weight_block_size=[128, 128],
+        )
+
+        logger.info_once(
+            "Loading w4afp8 checkpoint: routed experts via the W4A8 FP8 oracle "
+            "(INT4 g=%d x FP8-dynamic), dense Linear via FP8 block-128.",
+            group_size,
+        )
+        return inst
+
+    def apply_vllm_mapper(self, hf_to_vllm_mapper: WeightsMapper) -> None:
+        super().apply_vllm_mapper(hf_to_vllm_mapper)
+        self._dense_fp8_config.ignored_layers = hf_to_vllm_mapper.apply_list(
+            self._dense_fp8_config.ignored_layers
+        )
+
+    def get_quant_method(
+        self, layer: torch.nn.Module, prefix: str
+    ) -> QuantizeMethodBase | None:
+        from vllm.model_executor.layers.linear import LinearBase
+
+        if isinstance(layer, LinearBase):
+            return self._dense_fp8_config.get_quant_method(layer, prefix)
+
+        if isinstance(layer, RoutedExperts):
+            # Resolve the scheme through compressed-tensors, then swap in the
+            # adapter. The intermediate method object is cheap (backend
+            # selection only) and is discarded immediately.
+            base = super().get_quant_method(layer, prefix)
+            if isinstance(base, CompressedTensorsW4A8Fp8MoEMethod):
+                return _W4AFP8MoEAdapter(
+                    weight_quant=base.weight_quant,
+                    input_quant=base.input_quant,
+                    moe=layer.moe_config,
+                    layer_name=prefix,
+                )
+            if base is None:
+                # Running these experts unquantized would produce silent
+                # garbage, so make the mismatch visible.
+                logger.warning_once(
+                    "w4afp8: routed experts of %s are not quantized; the "
+                    "checkpoint layout does not match %s",
+                    prefix,
+                    _MOE_EXPERTS_TARGET,
+                )
+            return base
+
+        return super().get_quant_method(layer, prefix)
